points.requirement: Sequential A priming can induce B-receptor expression that persists after A; it does not require simultaneous A and B on every later target.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In cell-based examples, split and tuned activation/costimulation can implement an AND-like requirement, either-target recognition can broaden coverage with an OR-like rule, and a protective-antigen input can inhibit activity. points.requirement: Common first-, second- and third-generation labels describe zero, one and two costimulatory regions alongside activation, rather than an efficacy ranking.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Generation labels describe common signaling architectures. First-generation constructs use an activation domain, often CD3 zeta; second-generation designs add one costimulatory region; third-generation designs combine two. Fourth-generation and later labels vary across authors. More domains do not establish better patient outcomes. The full binder, spacer, anchor, signaling arrangement and cell preparation still matter.
evidence.explanation: Generation labels state zero, one or two costimulatory regions without establishing a clinical rank.

points.requirement: Identify the complete binder, spacer, anchor and signaling arrangement; matched-construct and cell-preparation comparisons are needed to attribute an effect to one change.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Suppose two fictional CARs differ only in their hinge: both bind purified antigen, but only one kills antigen-bearing cells. Compare surface expression and the geometry of cell contact before concluding that affinity is the problem. Likewise, DNA-positive cells without killing leave RNA production, receptor folding and trafficking, actual binding and signalling as separate possible failure points. Hudecek’s R11 ROR1 experiments illustrate a product-specific constraint: a long spacer enabled recognition of its membrane-proximal epitope, while changes that reduced Fc-receptor binding improved activity in the tested mice. Longer is not a universal design rule. Treat the transmembrane segment as part of the finished construct: assess assembly, surface expression and interactions rather than presume it is a neutral anchor. Unstimulated signalling and responses to repeated target encounters also need separate assessment.
evidence.explanation: The matched-hinge worked example separates binding, surface presentation, contact geometry and finished-cell performance.

evidence.explanation: Conventional surface recognition and the specified WT1 peptide-HLA CAR exception are separately qualified.

points.requirement: Distinguish drug-controlled signaling, engineered-cell elimination and resolution of previously initiated injury.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A living cell product can persist after administration stops. Activity switches regulate a defined function; elimination switches aim to remove cells. A drug-gated receptor may require a supplied molecule for signaling, whereas inducible caspase-9 activates a cell-death pathway when its dimerizing trigger is given. A removable surface tag offers another clearance route. These mechanisms need evidence within the actual finished product, including trigger exposure, speed, completeness and residual activity. None guarantees instant removal from every tissue or reversal of prior injury.

Di Stasi tested inducible caspase-9 in donor T cells after haploidentical stem-cell transplantation, rather than as a general CAR-T rescue trial. In the GD2-CART01 neuroblastoma report, the suicide switch was activated in one participant.
evidence.explanation: Defined activity control, elimination of living cells and reversal of downstream injury are explicitly distinct.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Name the controlled process and trigger, then measure receptor activity, viable engineered-cell abundance and downstream harms separately before and after triggering.

points.requirement: Name inducible caspase-9 and its AP1903 dimerizing trigger as a cell-elimination example, separate from the activity-switch exercise.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In the five-person Di Stasi study, four recipients developed graft-versus-host disease and received AP1903. The report describes a reduction exceeding 90% of modified T cells within half an hour and control of that disease. This is a specified transplant setting, not proof of complete whole-body clearance or reversal of every CAR-associated toxicity.
evidence.explanation: Inducible caspase-9 and AP1903 are tied to the original donor-T-cell transplant experiment.

points.requirement: Trigger access, leakage, speed, completeness, survivors and potential regrowth require product-specific tests; prior released signals and injury can persist.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Record the exact trigger, concentration, time and viable-cell input. Compare switch-positive and switch-negative cells and untriggered controls. Keep receptor signaling, secretion, proliferation, target-cell killing, absolute surviving cells and the surviving fraction distinct. A sequence check does not demonstrate a functional switch. Check baseline leakage, incomplete switch expression, survivors that regrow, and the trigger’s access to relevant tissues. Evaluate the switch after manufacture within the finished cell product; a sequence result cannot substitute for these functional tests.
evidence.explanation: The existing testing rule names trigger access, leakage, time, survivors, regrowth and residual injury rather than guaranteed rescue.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional matched blood measurement, 100 modified cells fall to five after a trigger, a 95 per cent reduction. A cytokine readout falls, but organ injury is unchanged. These are three different outcomes: sampled cell abundance, inflammatory signal and injury. Ask whether viable survivors retain receptor function, which tissues were sampled, when the measurements were made and whether survivors regrow. A sequence check or six people observed for four weeks without an event cannot establish a functioning rescue mechanism, complete body-wide clearance, zero risk or reversal of an injury already present. A usable control plan also depends on switch expression, trigger delivery to the relevant cells and access to the drug and specialist care; an encoded switch alone establishes none of these.
evidence.explanation: The existing testing rule names trigger access, leakage, time, survivors, regrowth and residual injury rather than guaranteed rescue.

points.requirement: A surface-target engager supplies a dosed protein recruiting available T cells, whereas this CAR-T comparison supplies receptor-bearing living cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Compared with administered CAR-T or TCR-T cells, a protein engager recruits effectors rather than supplying engineered responders. Protein mass/concentration and viable-cell dose have different units; clearance differs from cell survival, expansion and trafficking. A shared target name does not establish matched epitope, affinity, contact geometry, exposure, controllability or safety.
evidence.explanation: Dosed proteins recruit available effectors; the comparison CAR-T product supplies receptor-bearing living cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A receptor-bearing cell, its genetic instructions and its receptor protein are different objects. For a protein-coding instruction, DNA is transcribed into RNA, and a ribosome translates usable messenger RNA into protein. Delivered messenger RNA starts at the translation step. Folding and transport to the membrane still have to occur before a surface receptor can bind its target. In this schematic sequence, simplified shapes and an arrow from recognition toward a response do not show that every cell expressed the receptor or completed killing.
evidence.explanation: Dosed proteins recruit available effectors; the comparison CAR-T product supplies receptor-bearing living cells.

points.requirement: A shared fictional intact M target does not establish matched epitope, affinity, geometry, tissue exposure or performance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Compare recognition, T-cell activation, proliferation, target death, cytokine release and protein exposure at named times. Record effector source/state, target density, effector-to-target ratio, dose or concentration and denominator; include target-negative and no-effector controls. A granule or cytokine signal does not substitute for completed target-cell death or clinical benefit. Cytokines in a culture are a measured laboratory endpoint, not a diagnosis of clinical cytokine-release syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Shared fictional M binding leaves epitope, geometry, exposure and finished-product function unmeasured.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Binding, surface CAR expression, activation, proliferation and completed target-cell killing are distinct readouts. Compare otherwise matched constructs, target-positive and target-negative cells, healthy-tissue targets and unstimulated activity. Hudecek found that particular IgG-derived spacers could support killing in a dish yet impair activity in mouse models through Fc interactions.
evidence.explanation: Shared fictional M binding leaves epitope, geometry, exposure and finished-product function unmeasured.

points.requirement: The upper native lane has an extracellular M/CD3 bridge to recruited-cell CD3; the lower has an M-binding membrane CAR with signaling inside the administered cell.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A specified target-binding region and T-cell-recruiting region promote encounters. CD3 recruitment can bypass the recruited cell’s own antigen specificity; a peptide-HLA-binding target arm still retains its peptide and HLA requirements.
evidence.explanation: The two whole native lanes locate extracellular CD3 recruitment versus a membrane receptor with internal signaling.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region. Conventional surface-antigen recognition can bypass peptide-HLA presentation; specialized peptide-HLA-targeting CARs retain the relevant HLA and antigen-processing requirements.
evidence.explanation: The two whole native lanes locate extracellular CD3 recruitment versus a membrane receptor with internal signaling.

points.requirement: Protein concentration/distribution/clearance and cell delivery/survival/trafficking are different exposure questions and dose descriptions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Compared with administered CAR-T or TCR-T cells, a protein engager recruits effectors rather than supplying engineered responders. Protein mass/concentration and viable-cell dose have different units; clearance differs from cell survival, expansion and trafficking. A shared target name does not establish matched epitope, affinity, contact geometry, exposure, controllability or safety.
evidence.explanation: Protein mass/concentration, administered viable cells and later cellular abundance answer different exposure questions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: An administered cell dose is an input. The dose of a vector or particle used for in vivo engineering does not directly specify the later number of engineered cells. Autologous means the recipient’s own cells; allogeneic means cells from another person. Engineering outside versus inside the body is a separate axis; a prepared delivery product can engineer the recipient's own cells.
evidence.explanation: Protein mass/concentration, administered viable cells and later cellular abundance answer different exposure questions.

points.requirement: Binding observations in the fictional product cards and native contacts do not supply timed killing, healthy-tissue safety or an instantly reversible effect.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Compare recognition, T-cell activation, proliferation, target death, cytokine release and protein exposure at named times. Record effector source/state, target density, effector-to-target ratio, dose or concentration and denominator; include target-negative and no-effector controls. A granule or cytokine signal does not substitute for completed target-cell death or clinical benefit. Cytokines in a culture are a measured laboratory endpoint, not a diagnosis of clinical cytokine-release syndrome.
evidence.explanation: Binding alone does not establish timed killing or safety; stopping exposure does not guarantee prompt reversal of injury.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Stopping a protein infusion and reversing an injury are different outcomes. In Kebenko's 2018 phase 1 solitomab study of 65 patients with refractory solid tumours, the reported half-life was 4.5 hours. Diarrhoea limited dosing; one grade 3 event progressed to grade 5 after solitomab discontinuation. That observation shows why short measured protein exposure does not guarantee immediate reversal of toxicity. It is one product and study, not a rate or a safety rule for all engagers. Living engineered cells have their own expansion, persistence and trafficking, rather than sharing this protein's clearance clock.
evidence.explanation: Binding alone does not establish timed killing or safety; stopping exposure does not guarantee prompt reversal of injury.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy starts with cells collected from tumor tissue, commonly using their existing T-cell receptors. Infiltration does not prove that every cell recognizes the cancer. Culture and selection can change which clones become abundant; final viable-cell yield, recognition breadth and useful function need their own evidence. Manufacturing, conditioning, cytokine support and follow-up form a complete regimen with separate contributions and harms.

Lifileucel (Amtagvi) received accelerated FDA approval in 2024 for specified previously treated unresectable or metastatic melanoma. Its label defines the prior-treatment conditions and regimen. TILVANCE-301 is a phase 3 advanced-melanoma study of a lifileucel regimen with pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab. Neither a registry design nor clinical evidence from one TIL process establishes benefit for every tumor or manufacturing method.
evidence.explanation: Collection from tumour tissue does not establish the specificity of every infiltrating cell; human bystander evidence is scoped.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Simoni studied human lung and colorectal tumor infiltrates and found CD8 T cells recognizing viral epitopes unrelated to the cancer. evidence.explanation: Collection from tumour tissue does not establish the specificity of every infiltrating cell; human bystander evidence is scoped.
